reasons: The rule caps a Vendor-favourable audit right; the Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right against Customer, so the absence is more favourable than the preferred position and correctly recorded as compliant rather than a deviation or missing entitlement.

Cited text (Section 1) supports the rationale: the only access-flavoured language is a service-enablement cooperation covenant, not a right to examine Customer's books, usage or systems, and it contains no remote/system-access grant that would trigger walk-away territory.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was rendered and no counterparty comment was proposed; the failing 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a false signal because there is no audit clause to carry a frequency cap.
Rationale is accurate and appropriately notes the residual risk that Exhibits incorporated under Section 1 could later introduce audit or system-access language requiring the preferred parameters.
